_meta.indication: ADAKVEO is a selectin blocker indicated to reduce the frequency of vasoocclusive crises in adults and pediatric patients aged 16 years and older with sickle cell disease.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 2, randomized (1:1:1), multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study comparing crizanlizumab 5 mg/kg, crizanlizumab 2.5 mg/kg, and placebo by IV infusion at Week 0, Week 2, and every 4 weeks thereafter.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged 16 to 63 years with sickle cell disease (Hgb SS, SC, S/Beta0 Thalassemia, S/Beta+ Thalassemia) with a history of 2-10 vaso-occlusive crises in the previous 12 months.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annual rate of VOCs leading to a healthcare visit.
pivotal_trials.n: 198 patients randomized 1:1:1 (crizanlizumab 5 mg/kg N=67, crizanlizumab 2.5 mg/kg N=66, placebo N=65).
pivotal_trials.result: Median annual rate of VOC was 1.63 with ADAKVEO 5 mg/kg vs 2.98 with placebo (p=0.010). 36% of ADAKVEO patients had no VOC during the 52-week study vs 17% of placebo. Median time to first VOC was 4.1 months vs 1.4 months. Crizanlizumab 2.5 mg/kg was not statistically significant (2.01 vs 2.98, p=0.180).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >10%) were nausea (18% vs 11% placebo), arthralgia (18% vs 8%), back pain (15% vs 11%), and pyrexia (11% vs 7%). Serious adverse reactions were reported in 2 patients (3%) treated with ADAKVEO 5 mg/kg (both pyrexia). Infusion-related reactions occurred in 2 (3%) patients.
target_moa: Crizanlizumab-tmca is a humanized IgG2 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds to P-selectin and blocks interactions with its ligands including P-selectin glycoprotein ligand 1. P-selectin is an adhesion molecule expressed on activated endothelial cells and platelets critical in the initial recruitment of leukocytes and aggregation of platelets at sites of vascular occlusion.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not presented at an Advisory Committee; presentation was not needed because the Division is familiar with the endpoints, trial design, and control arms.
